title: SLO deconstruction for mixed-latency endpoints with prioritized eviction and region-aware circuit breakers
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Several customer-facing LLM routes (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-batch) show different tail-latency and quality failure modes during regional capacity pressure. Existing SLOs are monolithic (per-service) and cause blunt failover and global throttles. We need a per-endpoint + per-model SLO decomposition that supports: 1) prioritized eviction (tenant-aware, SL-based) 2) region-aware circuit breakers (graceful regional degradation before global failover) 3) explicit error budget borrowing and repayment rules.
background: Current incidents: two incidents in Q4 2024 where embeddings-batch northamerica saturations triggered global variant downgrade causing high-quality regressions for enterprise tenants. Post-mortem pointed to coarse SLOs and missing per-endpoint error budget accounting. We have strong observability (request-level traces, per-model token counts, tail latencies) but lack canonical SLI formulas mapped to policy actions.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical SLI formulas for: availability (p99-success-rate), request-level latency (p95/p99), quality (promptset-based correctness rate) for chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-batch
Document error budget accounting: per-endpoint, per-model-variant, and tenant-weighted allocations with borrow/repay flows
Design region-aware circuit breaker thresholds and step-down actions (variant degrade -> route-level throttling -> regional ejection)
Implement a prototype circuit-breaker config schema and validation (schema + example rules in runtime-config repo)
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules mapping SLI breaches -> error-budget burn -> operator runbook steps
Run tabletop failure drill with on-call and SRE to validate runbook for prioritized eviction and failover
Ship rollout plan with canary (10% traffic) and automated rollback conditions
Unit/integration tests for SLI calculations and simulator-based verification of circuit-breaker transitions
design_decisions: Use request-success-rate (status=200 && model-ok) as availability SLI, measured over 5m and 1h windows. Use 5m window for circuit-breaker fast-path, 1h for error-budget accounting
Tail latency SLI: p99 of request end-to-end (ingress->egress), with token-normalized thresholds per route (chat-long has higher expected p99)
Quality SLI: use existing eval promptsets per route (daily sampled) to compute rolling correctness rate; initial target is 98% for chat-short, 95% for chat-long, 99% for embeddings-batch recall proxy
Borrowing: endpoints may borrow up to 30% of adjacent non-critical route budgets (configurable), with repay window 72h; borrow requires explicit approval for >50% of endpoint budget

Prioritized eviction: eviction order = (1) best-effort background jobs, (2) bulk embeddings batch lower-priority tenants, (3) guest/free-tier chat, (4) paid/enterprise pinned slots; eviction decisions use tenant weight + SLA tier
Circuit-breaker transitions will be stateful per-region and per-model-variant. States: CLOSED -> FAST-TAIL WARNING -> PARTIAL_DEGRADE (variant fallback) -> THROTTLE -> EJECT_REGION
Load-shedding choices: prefer downgrade (lower-capacity model variant) > token-limit truncation > queueing > outright reject for latency-critical routes

Use Grafana + Alertmanager + on-call chatops (Slack) for operator signals. Automated actions (degrade/evict) require a two-step validation: metric trigger + soft approval window unless emergency flag is set

monitoring: Primary signals: slo.availability.{route}.{model_variant} (5m,1h), slo.latency.p95/p99.{route}.{region}, slo.quality.promptset.{route}. Secondary signals: hosts.cpu/gpu_util, queue_depth, kv_cache_hit_rate. Alerting cadence: fast alerts at 5m burn rate, pager when 5m burn implies >50% daily error budget consumption.
policy_snippets: Circuit-breaker fast path: if 5m error rate > 3x baseline threshold AND p99 latency > config.threshold -> enter FAST-TAIL WARNING. After two consecutive 5m windows in WARNING, trigger PARTIAL_DEGRADE. PARTIAL_DEGRADE: switch model_variant -> degraded_variant for up to 15m; if error budget continues to burn, escalate to THROTTLE with token-based rate limit per-tenant and then EJECT_REGION. Eviction policy: compute eviction_score = tenant_weight * (1 - sla_priority) * recent_token_usage; evict highest score first. Borrow/repay: borrowed_budget must be listed in incident log and auto-repaid from the next three 24h windows unless override.
runbook: 1) On alert '5m error budget burn >50% projected', notify SRE + oncall; 2) Check grafana panel for affected routes and region; 3) If in FAST-TAIL WARNING -> monitor one more 5m window; 4) If transition to PARTIAL_DEGRADE, notify product owners and enable degraded_variant routing (automated if configured); 5) If THROTTLE, enable tenant-aware rate limits and start prioritized eviction controller; 6) If EJECT_REGION, failover traffic to secondary region and mark region for capacity rebuild; 7) Post-incident: file borrow entries and schedule repay, update runbook with lessons
testing_strategy: Unit tests for SLI formula functions, end-to-end simulator tests that replay historical incidents with synthetic increases in tail latency, chaos test that terminates a region and verifies state transitions and canary rollback. Add smoke test in CI to validate runtime-config schema parsing.
